# `silk/crypto/sha2`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Compute SHA-2 digests: SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-512/224, and SHA-512/256.

## When to use
Use [`Sha256`](#Sha256) when you need a cryptographic hash and the protocol does not name another one.
Use the type that a protocol names, for example [`Sha384`](#Sha384) for some TLS cipher suites. Use
`silk.crypto.hmac` for a keyed tag and `silk.collections.hash` for the keys of a hash map.

## Details
Each type has the same functions: `hash` returns the digest of one slice, and `make`, `update`,
and `finish` hash a message that arrives in parts. [`Sha256.checkpoint`](#Sha256.impl.checkpoint) and
[`Sha384.checkpoint`](#Sha384.impl.checkpoint) return the digest so far and keep the state. The states are fixed-size
values and nothing allocates. Digests use the standard big-endian byte order.

| Type | Digest | Block |
|------|--------|-------|
| [`Sha224`](#Sha224) | 28 bytes | 64 bytes |
| [`Sha256`](#Sha256) | 32 bytes | 64 bytes |
| [`Sha384`](#Sha384) | 48 bytes | 128 bytes |
| [`Sha512`](#Sha512) | 64 bytes | 128 bytes |
| [`Sha512_224`](#Sha512_224) | 28 bytes | 128 bytes |
| [`Sha512_256`](#Sha512_256) | 32 bytes | 128 bytes |

## Gotchas
`finish` consumes the state. To hash two messages that share a prefix, use `checkpoint`, or copy
the state before `finish`. Do not hash a secret key and a message together to make a tag. Use
`silk.crypto.hmac`.

## Examples
### Hash a message in one call and in parts
```silk
import silk.crypto.sha2 { Sha256 }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let oneShot = Sha256.hash(b"abc")
  let mut state = Sha256.make()
  state.update(b"a")
  state.update(b"bc")
  let streamed = state.finish()

  // SHA-256("abc") is ba7816bf...15ad.
  if oneShot[0] != 0xba || oneShot[31] != 0xad || streamed[0] != oneShot[0] {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

### Take a running digest with checkpoint
```silk
import silk.crypto.sha2 { Sha256 }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut transcript = Sha256.make()
  transcript.update(b"abc")
  let early = transcript.checkpoint()
  transcript.update(b"def")
  let full = transcript.finish()
  if early[0] != Sha256.hash(b"abc")[0] || full[0] != Sha256.hash(b"abcdef")[0] {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

## `Sha224`

```silk
pub struct Sha224
```

A streaming SHA-224 state that returns a 28-byte digest.

Call [`Sha224.update`](#Sha224.impl.update) for each part of the message, then [`Sha224.finish`](#Sha224.impl.finish). Use [`Sha224.hash`](#Sha224.impl.hash)
when the full message is in one slice. The state is a fixed-size value and does not allocate.

<a id="Sha224.impl"></a>

## Implementation `Sha224`

```silk
impl Sha224
```

<a id="Sha224.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make() -> Sha224
```

Returns a SHA-224 state for an empty message.

<a id="Sha224.impl.update"></a>

### Method `update`

```silk
pub fn update(self: &mut Self, bytes: &[u8]) -> ()
```

Adds `bytes` to the end of the message.

Any split of the message into parts gives the same digest. An empty slice changes nothing.

#### Gotchas
The program traps if the full message is longer than 2^64 - 1 bits.

<a id="Sha224.impl.finish"></a>

### Method `finish`

```silk
pub fn finish(self: Self) -> [u8; 28]
```

Returns the 28-byte SHA-224 digest of the message and consumes the state.

<a id="Sha224.impl.hash"></a>

### Associated function `hash`

```silk
pub fn hash(bytes: &[u8]) -> [u8; 28]
```

Returns the 28-byte SHA-224 digest of `bytes`.

#### Gotchas
The program traps if `bytes` is longer than 2^64 - 1 bits.
